algarve.overview: The Algarve is known for its dramatic coastal hiking, led by the moderate Seven Hanging Valleys trail that traces limestone cliffs and sea caves above the Atlantic. For multi-day routes, the Fishermen's Trail is an 11- to 13-day coastal trek of about 135 miles along the rugged western edge, while the 186-mile Via Algarviana crosses the inland hills in 14 stages. The exposed coastal paths have little shade, making spring and autumn the best times to walk, while summer heat requires starting at dawn.

months.6: Summer heat sets in, making the unshaded coastal paths strenuous by midday. Start early to finish before the afternoon heat.
months.8: The hottest month offers little relief on the shadeless coastal routes. Start at dawn, as midday on the unshaded cliffs is very hot.

amsterdam.overview: The Netherlands is famously flat, so the walking within reach of the city is easy and mostly paved or graded. The best routes are under an hour away in Zuid-Kennemerland National Park, where moderate paths wind through coastal dunes to the North Sea beach.

andalucia.overview: Hiking ranges from the high peaks of the Sierra Nevada to deep limestone gorges, with the Caminito del Rey as the headline route. Pinned to the sheer walls of the Gaitanes Gorge, this moderate walk requires a timed ticket, and most visitors take a shuttle to the start. The high mountains offer strenuous day hikes to summits like Mulhacén. The hiking is best in spring and autumn, as summer heat is extreme.

months.7: Heavy downpours leave multi-day treks wet and leech-ridden, with flooded trails; short, easy walks are the practical choice.

months.6: Highs climb into the 90s and can top 100°F, making the exposed sandstone dangerous by midday. Hikers must start at dawn and finish strenuous routes by mid-morning.
months.8: The intense heat continues, with the added possibility of late-summer afternoon thunderstorms causing flash floods in narrow canyons. Early morning is the best time to walk.

argentine-lake-district.overview: The Argentine Lake District is known for its mountain trails through southern beech forests to granite spires and alpine lakes. The hiking centers on Nahuel Huapi National Park near Bariloche, where day hikes reach viewpoints over the lakes and a network of mountain huts supports multi-day treks. The long hike to Refugio Frey is the headline route, climbing to a cirque of jagged peaks and a high lake. A free national park registration is required for the trails, and the refugios must be booked in advance.

months.1: The trails are clear of snow, and the refugios are fully open. The long hike to Refugio Frey and the multi-day hut-to-hut routes are at their best.
months.2: The high trails and passes are clear, and the refugios are open. The long hike to Refugio Frey and the multi-day hut-to-hut routes are at their best.
months.3: The trails are clear, and the refugios remain open. The long hike to Refugio Frey and the multi-day hut-to-hut routes are working well.
months.5: Snow closes the high passes and the multi-day hut-to-hut routes. The hike to Refugio Frey turns snowy and slow, and only the lower forest trails remain clear.
months.6: Deep snow covers the mountains. The high trails are closed and the last stretch to Refugio Frey is under snow, leaving mostly short, snowy walks in the lower valleys.
months.7: Deep snow covers the mountains. The high trails are closed and the last stretch to Refugio Frey is under snow, leaving mostly short, snowy walks in the lower valleys.
months.8: Deep snow covers the mountains. The high trails are closed and the last stretch to Refugio Frey is under snow, leaving mostly short, snowy walks in the lower valleys.
months.9: The snow begins to melt in the lower valleys, opening some moderate forest trails, but the high passes and the upper stretch of the Refugio Frey hike remain snowbound.
months.10: The lower trails are clear, and the hike to Refugio Frey is walkable with snow patches. The high passes still hold snow, and the multi-day hut-to-hut routes are only starting to open.
months.12: The trails are mostly clear of snow, and the refugios open for the season. The long hike to Refugio Frey and the multi-day hut-to-hut routes are working well.

azores.overview: Volcanic craters, coastal cliffs and lush laurel forests define the hiking on these mid-Atlantic islands. The headline route is the strenuous climb up Mount Pico, Portugal's highest peak, which rewards hikers with panoramic ocean views. Other highlights include the trails around Faial's Caldeira crater and the paths circling the twin lakes of Sete Cidades. The trails are walkable year-round, though rain frequently obscures the heights.

months.5: Clearer skies make the moderate crater rim walks more reliable for expansive views. The steep climb up Mount Pico is open, though the summit can still catch passing clouds.
months.6: Long daylight hours and mostly clear skies provide excellent conditions for the high volcanic routes. The strenuous climb up Mount Pico rewards hikers with expansive mid-Atlantic views, while the coastal paths remain breezy and moderate.
months.9: The trails remain largely dry and the volcanic slopes are bright green. The strenuous ascent of Mount Pico and the trails around Faial's Caldeira crater offer excellent visibility and steady walking conditions.

bagan.overview: Hiking here focuses on village-to-village routes through agricultural landscapes and forested hills, best known for the moderate two- to three-day trek from Kalaw to Inle Lake. Day hikes explore the hills around Hsipaw or the slopes of Mount Victoria. The routes pass through rural communities and tea plantations, earning views of the rolling countryside, with the best conditions during the cooler, dry months.

bali.overview: Bali's hiking centers on its volcanic peaks and lush interior. The headline route is the moderate Mount Batur sunrise hike, which requires a local guide arranged at the trailhead to navigate the dark, rocky path to the crater rim. Easier walking weaves through the island's famous rice terraces and jungle waterfalls. The trails are best from April to October when the ground is dry and the summit views are clear.

bavaria-munich.overview: The real walking is about an hour and a half south of the city in the Bavarian Alps, where trains and cable cars lift hikers to high ridge trails above alpine lakes. The network around Garmisch and Mittenwald offers everything from easy valley loops to strenuous limestone summits and multi-day hut-to-hut routes.

months.7: The entire alpine network is clear and at its best. The trails around Eibsee and Walchensee are crowded, with heavy traffic.
months.8: High summer brings perfect conditions on the ridges. Expect crowded trails and heavy traffic at the popular Eibsee and Walchensee trailheads.

bhutan.overview: Bhutan offers some of the most dramatic and remote walking in the Himalayas, from steep forest day hikes to legendary high-altitude expedition treks. The steep climb to the cliffside Tiger's Nest monastery is the headline day hike, while the multi-week Snowman Trek and the shorter Druk Path Trek cross remote passes beneath unclimbed peaks. All hiking requires a licensed guide and a daily fee, keeping the trails pristine. The best walking is in spring and autumn.

borneo.overview: Rainforest trails and the ascent of Mount Kinabalu are the main draws here. The Kinabalu climb is a strenuous two-day trek to a 13,435-foot granite summit, requiring a mandatory guide, a permit, and an overnight stay. Lower down, day hikers explore the jungle paths of Bako National Park and the Danum Valley to reach canopy walkways and coastal cliffs. The trails are hot and humid year-round, with the best footing outside the monsoon.

months.1: The northeast monsoon brings heavy rain and muddy trails to the rainforest. The Mount Kinabalu summit climb can be closed at short notice by dangerous weather, making this a tough time for walkers.
months.12: Heavy monsoon rains make for difficult walking conditions. Rainforest paths are slick, and the strenuous Mount Kinabalu trek can be closed at short notice by summit weather.

budapest.overview: The Buda Hills rise directly above the city, offering a network of easy to moderate forest trails. Hikers can reach the trailheads by bus or the historic cogwheel railway to walk the popular ridge paths around Normafa and János-hegy. The highest point provides panoramic views over the city.
